findings.text: Ask 4, the cross-family review, is not done. Nobody has run `Server/review.mjs --model <openrouter slug>` on a real recent task and compared it with the same-model review. task.jsonl:1 lists it only as a planned step, and the diff adds just a comment at Server/review.mjs:666. That comparison is the owner's second reason for this work (a consensus from other model families), so it has to run before the task lands.

The real cost usually comes out as $0. Billing on OpenRouter takes a few seconds to settle, and `refresh_or_cost()` (Agents.js:1091) reads the key total right when the turn ends. So each turn shows the previous turn's spend, and the last turn's spend never shows at all; a one-shot reviewer would show $0. spike.jsonl:739 already shows this: deepseek's total is $0 for two real turns. Re-read the total a few seconds after the turn ends, or poll until it changes, so that the dashboard shows the real cost as ask 2 requires.

The spike's cost-per-turn result can't be trusted for the same reason: four of its six rows report $0 for a turn that did work. Add a short wait before each `key_usage()` read in spike.mjs (lines 666 and 676), then re-run the spike once so ask 1's "cost per turn" has real numbers.

The "id never matches" conclusion is wrong. spike.jsonl:743 (gemini-3.8-flash) has `generation_id_matches_message_id: true`, but the minion's log (wire-provider/task.jsonl:795) and the readme say it never matches. Where the id does match, `generation_cost()` returns an exact per-turn figure that doesn't depend on the shared key total. Worth a second look before settling on the before/after diff.

The tiers.js comment at line 180 says "Agents.spawn() already reads this `provider` field", which isn't true. Roles take only `model(tier)` (roles.js:21), and spawn picks the provider by the slash rule on the model id. The new `provider` export (tiers.js:190) has no callers. It works anyway, because an OpenRouter slug always contains a `/`. Either make the comment say that, or have roles copy the tier's `provider` too.

Nothing prevents `provider: "openrouter"` with a `claude-*` model. That would bill Claude per token through the gateway, which requirements.md rules out ("Claude itself stays on the subscription"). A one-line refusal in `Agents.spawn()` (Agents.js:107) would enforce the rule.

Some of the readme is out of date now. Point 2 (Servex/ext/openrouter/readme.md:14) still says "nothing reads" the provider field, and point 3 (readme.md:17) says "OpenRouter puts the real dollar cost on every reply", which contradicts the key-total diff that was actually built. Both should match what the code does now.

Simpler: `real_cost()` in provider.js has no callers, and `has_key()`'s comment says door() uses it, which it doesn't (only spike.mjs does). Delete the dead export and fix the comment. Also, `COST_CAP_USD` in spike.mjs:573 is only reported, never enforced; the only real cap is `maxTurns`.

Asks 1–3 are otherwise met. GPT, DeepSeek and Gemini Flash each completed Read, Bash and Edit, with streaming and a working resume. The provider can be set per spawn and is kept on resume, and the Gemini `ArtifactData` schema 400 was correctly worked around with `disallowedTools`. Compaction through the proxy has not been tested yet; it stays an open question in the readme.

The cross-family comparison is missing (requirement 1.4): Server/review.mjs:666–669 in diff.patch adds only a comment; there is no recorded run on a recent task alongside a same-model review.

The phase-two evaluation is absent from this patch (requirements 2.2–2.5 and 2b): it contains no known-answer rule tests, effort-level cost table, model-by-task matrix, probe-result log, or brainstorm-and-rate naming run. The Read/Bash/Edit spike tests SDK compatibility, not whether agents follow this project's rules or build a working page.

A tier's provider is not actually the switch (requirement 1.2): tiers.js:190 in diff.patch exports `provider`, but the patch has no caller for it; Agents.js:35 chooses by model slash instead. Moving a tier's provider alone therefore does nothing; either pass it from role defaults or describe the slash rule as the sole switch.

The spike mislabels a failed resume as a pass (requirement 1.1): spike.mjs:719–729 prints `resume ok` from `!is_error` without checking the answer; spike.jsonl:743 has an empty Gemini Flash resume answer marked successful. Verify that the response names red and blue before counting it.

An explicit `provider: "openrouter"` can be paired with a Claude model in Agents.js:35 of diff.patch, contrary to requirements.md:13 that Claude stay on the subscription. Refusing that combination is simpler than relying on every caller to remember the billing boundary.

provider.js:321–330 in diff.patch exports `real_cost()` but Agents.js implements a separate key-difference calculation; use one cost path. The readme's claims at lines 426–431 also still describe the provider field as unread and real cost as attached to every reply, unlike the patch.

findings.text: Each keys-to-success page opens with the raw dictated prompt, and the answer the page exists to show (the consensus keys and each model's score) sits below it, one to three screens down (page 1, presentation rule "level 1 shown, detail nested"). Evidence: `shots/…keys-to-success-research-process-fast-assistants/1920.png`, where the prompt fills the whole first screen. layout.json gives the page-keys-test band a share of 3.59 at 400 and 2.75 at 1920. Fix: put the keys and the score table first, and move the prompt below them or into a collapsed block.

The keys-to-success index and its child pages use the URL slug as their title: "bigger", "unsupported-link", "research-process-fast-assistants". Their sibling tests have real names, like "H1 page" and "Broken import" (words: names can't be misread). The index cards carry no description either, so a reader can't tell what any prompt is about without opening it. Evidence: `shots/…keys-to-success/1200.png`, the preview wall. In the diff, line 1 of each page.jsonl reads `"title":"bigger"`.

The slug titles also wrap to two lines on most child pages at 400, and on two of them at every width. layout.json reports `h1.page-title` at 2 lines on cards-and-logs-subdomain and research-process-fast-assistants at 1200, 1920 and 3440. A short plain-words title fixes this together with finding 2.

The Test library index preview for "Keys to success" is the only card with a description, so it stands taller than the five tests beside it. Evidence: `shots/…framework-ai-tests/1920.png`, top band. Giving every test a one-line description, or none, would make the wall even.

The 12 `test-library/runs/h1-page-*` shots are fixtures that models wrote during the tests. Most show an empty "Floor test" page: layout.json gives page-previews a share of 0 and 85–94% of the screen is empty. That is expected for a test fixture. They are not pages for readers, so their design was not judged.
The `drawer-rail` and `mode-btn` buttons wrap (1.7–3.2 lines) on every page, at every width. That comes from the shared site chrome, not from this diff.
